1|"""Investigation: break a MobileMoE-S decode step into pieces and time each one.
2|
3|Each process runs one engine on the int4 model and appends one JSON line per
4|run to runs-<engine>.jsonl in the output folder:
5|
6|  plain   the mlx_lm port with its own KV cache, pipelined like mlx_lm generate
7|  vllm    vLLM in process: vllm-metal's model runner, paged attention, sampler
8|
9|Wrappers installed at runtime give each piece of the step a named span (the
10|model's layers, attention and expert parts, and in vLLM the runner's own
11|steps). Every run uses one mode:
12|
13|  bare        only the step-boundary hooks: the step period as served
14|  off         all wrappers installed but idle: the baseline for knock-outs
15|  cpu         spans timed, nothing else changed: CPU time of each piece

17|              exit, so its kernels are encoded and run on their own: encoding
18|              (CPU) and GPU time per piece. One step also exports each piece's

25|              the piece still runs. At 1 row the step is CPU-bound, so the

172|    def maybe_census(self, rows, prefill):
173|        """In sync mode, count the operations of one steady step."""

179|    def replay(self, name, fn, args, kwargs):
180|        """Knock-out: the first output for inputs of this shape, without running.

183|        plain engine's attention reads a key/value cache that grows each step.

189|            out = fn(*args, **kwargs)
190|            if self.control:

207|        if self.mode == "sync":  # the parent's pending work is the parent's

209|        cpu = time.thread_time() if name in CPU_TIMED else None

213|            out = fn(*args, **kwargs)
214|            if self.mode == "sync":
215|                self._sync(frame, arrays(out))

450|def prefill(model, ids, cache):

Replacement must keep: output layout exactly `[R,4,768]` bf16 with slot `j` ↔ `inds[r,j]` pairing [check_candidate.py:112-130](bench/grader/check_candidate.py) (note the checker maps flat index `j` to `(k,d)=divmod(j,768)` [check_candidate.py:126](bench/grader/check_candidate.py)); identical sort/no-sort threshold behavior is internal, but numerics must hold on both paths (grader tests R=1/8 → no-sort and R=32 → sort [check_candidate.py:26,179](bench/grader/check_candidate.py)).

- **Invariants.** Same experts G2 as Piece F (2 ulp, floor 0.001) [check_candidate.py:112-138](bench/grader/check_candidate.py).

### Piece D — `_gather_sort` [switch_layers.py:12-17](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py) (R=32 only)

- **Callers.** `SwitchGLU.__call__` iff `do_sort` [switch_layers.py:184-185](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py); `ref_experts` iff `inds.size>=64` [slots.py:62-65](bench/grader/slots.py). Runs at R=32 (128 pairs), not at R=1/8.
- **Callees.** `flatten→view`, `argsort→ArgSort` (×2: order, inv_order), `//M→FloorDivide`, two `[]→Gather` (rows, indices) — §1c; kernel names [tables.md:136](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md).
- **Data.** In: `x` [32,1,1,768] bf16, `indices` [32,4] uint32. Out: sorted rows [128,1,768] bf16 (consumer: the 3 sorted `gather_qmm`s), sorted `idx` [128] uint32, `inv_order` [128] (consumer: Piece E). `M=4` from `indices.shape` [switch_layers.py:13](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py).
- **Neighbours.** Before: expand_dims. After: sorted projs + activation + down proj, then Piece E. Replacement must keep: pairing of each sorted row with its expert index; `inv_order` exact inverse (`argsort(argsort)`) so unscrambling restores `inds` order.
- **Cost.** Kernels: 5/layer at R=32 (2 ArgSort + 1 FloorDivide + 2 Gather); ×20 = 40 + 20 + 40 of the step's sort overhead [tables.md:136,154](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md). Bytes: order/inv 128×4 B each; sorted rows 128×768×2 = 196,608 B/layer — arithmetic shown. Time: folded into experts 14.67 ms at 32 rows [tables.md:334](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md); the `experts`-span serialized GPU cost (sort+activation, excl. projs) is 4.11 ms plain at 32 rows vs 0.97 ms at 1 row [tables.md:259,210](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md).
- **Invariants.** Exact permutation (no numerics); downstream G2 is the experts 2-ulp rule.

### Piece E — `_scatter_unsort` [switch_layers.py:20-24](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py) (R=32 only)

- **Callers.** `SwitchGLU.__call__` after down proj iff `do_sort` [switch_layers.py:196-197](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py); `ref_experts` [slots.py:80-81](bench/grader/slots.py). R=32 only.
- **Callees.** `x[inv_order]→Gather`; `unflatten→view`; final `squeeze→view` in caller.
- **Data.** In: sorted down-output [128,1,768] bf16 + `inv_order` [128]. Out: [32,4,1,768] → squeeze → [32,4,768] bf16, consumer = combine [slots.py:116](bench/grader/slots.py).
- **Neighbours.** Before: down `gather_qmm`. After: squeeze + combine. Must restore exact `inds`-order pairing (slot j ↔ `inds[r,j]`).
- **Cost.** Kernels: 1/layer at R=32 (Gather); the 3rd/layer of the step's 60 `experts`-span Gathers [tables.md:136](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md). Bytes: read+write 128×768×2 = 196,608 B each per layer — arithmetic shown. Time folded into experts totals (Piece F).
- **Invariants.** Exact permutation; downstream experts G2.

### Piece F — Served expert projs: `TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear.__call__` [mobilemoe.py:172-184](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py) → `mx.gather_qmm`

- **Callers.** `SwitchGLU.__call__` 3× per layer (up, gate, down) [switch_layers.py:188-194](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py); `ref_experts.qmm` 3× [slots.py:67-79](bench/grader/slots.py). Shapes: no-sort `a` [R,1,1,768] (gate/up) / [R,4,1,384] (down input = activation), `rhs_indices` [R,4]; sort `a` [128,1,…], `idx` [128]. R=1 → 4 pairs; R=8 → 32 pairs; R=32 → 128 pairs.
- **Callees.** `mx.gather_qmm→GatherQMM` + internal `reshape(arange(n))→Arange` for default lhs indices [step-breakdown.md:423](claude/findings/step-breakdown.md) (1 Arange per proj: 3/layer, 60/step [tables.md:137-139](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md)). Below 60 rows/step MLX picks the per-pair kernel (from the code: `quantized.cpp`, MLX 0.32.4 [bottleneck-explained.md:175](claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md)); the grouped kernel needs sorted + pairs/experts ≥ 4 [moe_parts.py:149-150](bench/micro/moe_parts.py).
- **Data.** Per §1c + weight layouts: gate/up `w` [60,768,48] u32, scales/biases [60,768,12] bf16; down `w` [60,384,96], scales/biases [60,384,24] [brief.md:76-79](claude/muse-agent-brief.md). `w = scale*q + bias`, `q` 4-bit at word `o/8`, bits `4*(o%8)` [brief.md:82](claude/muse-agent-brief.md). Accumulate f32, round each product's output to bf16 [brief.md:90](claude/muse-agent-brief.md). Gate/up outputs [R,4,1,384] bf16 → activation; down output [R,4,1,768] bf16 → (unsort) → `y` [R,4,768].
- **Neighbours.** Before: (sorted) `x` / activation output. Between gate/up and down: fused silu-multiply (Piece G). After: combine. Replacement must keep the three-product contract `y[r,j]=(silu(x[r]@Wg[e])*(x[r]@Wu[e]))@Wd[e]`, `e=inds[r,j]` [brief.md:84-88](claude/muse-agent-brief.md), and the bf16 rounding points (below).
- **Cost.** Kernels: 6/layer (3× Arange+GatherQMM) both paths [tables.md:137-139](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md); +Piece C/D/E/G = 7 (R=1/8) / 13 (R=32) per layer. Weight bytes (arithmetic shown): per matrix per expert = `294,912×0.5 + (294,912/32)×4 = 147,456+36,864 = 184,320 B`; per expert `3×184,320 = 552,960 B` [bottleneck-explained.md:143-150](claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md) (768×384=294,912). Per-pair reads per step: R×4×20×552,960 = 44,236,800 B (44.2 MB) at R=1; 353,894,400 B (353.9 MB) at R=8; 1,415,577,600 B (1415.6 MB ≈1416 MB) at R=32. Distinct-once: 4.0/20.0/40.1 avg distinct/layer (R=1/8/32) [tables.md:399-401](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md); R=32 total 802 combos → `802×552,960 = 443,473,920 B ≈ 443.5 MB` [bottleneck-explained.md:161-173](claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md). Counter DRAM: 51 MB saved at R=1, 908 MB at R=32 [counters tables.md:26,32](results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md), i.e. extra over needed `908−443 = 465 MB` reached memory, rest from cache [bottleneck-explained.md:177-183](claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md). Effective 908 MB / 14.67 ms = 61.9 ≈ 62 GB/s (31% of 200) [bottleneck-explained.md:185-194](claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md). Activations per layer: gate/up/act 3× R×4×384×2 = R×9,216 B; out R×6,144 B. Measured time (knock-out, plain): **0.92 ms/step at R=1** (46 µs/layer), **14.67 ms/step at R=32** (733.5 µs/layer) [tables.md:334](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md) row `experts` — half the 28.19 ms step [tables.md:19](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md).
- **Invariants.** Experts G2: 2 bf16 ulp, floor at 0.001, same formula as combine [check_candidate.py:44-48,112-138](bench/grader/check_candidate.py). Rounding points: each of the 3 products accumulates f32 → rounds to bf16; `silu(gate)*up` computed on those bf16 values and rounded to bf16 before down [brief.md:90](claude/muse-agent-brief.md). Plus end-to-end: same greedy tokens over 24 tokens at 1 and 32 requests in plain MLX and vLLM [brief.md:185](claude/muse-agent-brief.md).

### Piece G — Activation: `swiglu` [activations.py:9-11](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/activations.py) via `SwiGLU` [switch_layers.py:152-157](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py)

`swiglu(gate,x) = silu(gate)*x`, `@partial(mx.compile, shapeless=True)` [activations.py:9-11](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/activations.py); called as `self.activation(x_up, x_gate)` = `swiglu(gate=x_gate, x=x_up)` [switch_layers.py:190-192,156-157](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py).

- **Callers.** `SwitchGLU.__call__` once/layer [switch_layers.py:190-192](third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py); `ref_experts` (`swiglu(qmm gate, qmm up)` [slots.py:79](bench/grader/slots.py)). Shapes: [R,4,1,384] no-sort (R=1/8), [128,1,384] sorted (R=32); bf16 in/out.
- **Callees.** Fused `CompiledSigmoidBroadcastBroadcastMultiplyBroadcastBroadcastMultiply` (sigmoid + 2 multiplies in one kernel: `silu(g)=g*sigmoid(g)`, then `×up`) — 20/step both paths [tables.md:136,141](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md). (Shared expert's identical op name [tables.md:141](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md) is its own span, not this piece.)
- **Data.** In: gate/up bf16 products. Out: bf16 [same shape], consumer = down proj. Intermediate f32/fused details are inside the compiled kernel; contract is the rounded bf16 result [brief.md:90](claude/muse-agent-brief.md).
- **Neighbours.** Between gate/up projs and down proj. Replacement must keep input pairing (gate vs up) and bf16 output.
- **Cost.** 1 kernel/layer (20/step) [tables.md:136](results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md); bytes ≈ 3× R×4×384×2 (2 reads + 1 write) = R×9,216 B/layer (+128-row sorted form at R=32). Time folded into experts totals (Piece F).
- **Invariants.** Covered by experts G2 (2 ulp on final `y`, not on the activation directly).

1|# Brief for the Muse Spark agent: write a faster MobileMoE-S decode kernel
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. Committed and tagged `agent-era` before the Muse Spark session started. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|You are a Claude Code session powered by Meta's Muse Spark, working in your own git worktree on the branch `muse-agent`. This brief fixes your task, what you may change, where your work goes and how it is judged. It does not change during your session.
6|
7|## The task
8|
9|Meta's MobileMoE-S, int4, is served on an Apple M1 Pro (16-core GPU, 200 GB/s, 16 GB) by vLLM through vllm-metal, which runs the model with MLX. The findings below measure where each decode step's time goes. A step is about 870–1,090 small GPU kernels and is far from both the bandwidth and compute limits. The findings name the pieces that cost the most.
10|
11|1. **Choose.** Read the findings and choose one or two of the slots below to replace with your own fused Metal kernels. Write `muse-spark/strategy.md`: why, your design, and what each saves per step at 1 and 32 requests (your estimate). End it with the JSON block described under *Your files*. Commit it.
12|2. **Write and check.** For each chosen slot, write the kernels as files, run the grader on them, read its verdict, and improve. Up to **5 attempts per slot**; an attempt is a folder you graded and committed.
13|3. **Finish.** Write `muse-spark/summary.md`: your final attempt per slot and what you learned. Commit it.
14|
15|**Read these first** (all in your worktree):
16|- `claude/findings/bottleneck-explained.md` and `claude/findings/step-breakdown.md`: the measured findings;
17|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
18|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
19|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
20|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
21|
22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
93|
94|## Tools and limits
95|
96|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
97|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
98|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes; stop one that hangs.
99|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
100|
101|## Rules of this session
102|
103|These keep your work apart from everyone else's. Git hooks and an audit script enforce them, and a commit that breaks them is refused.
104|
105|- **Write only inside `muse-spark/`.** Never change `bench/`, `claude/`, `results/`, `tools/`, `third_party/`, or any other file. A copy of the grader you edit is never used.
106|- **Commit only on `muse-agent`,** with the co-author trailer your settings add: `Co-Authored-By: Muse Spark (Meta Model API) <muse-spark@meta-model-api.invalid>`. Start each subject with `Muse Spark:`. No other co-author.
107|- **Never push, merge, rebase, change git config, or skip hooks.**
108|- **Don't read `.env`** or any credentials file.
109|- One commit per attempt, after you've run the grader on it, so the history shows every attempt in order.
110|
111|## Your files
112|
113|```
114|muse-spark/
115|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
116|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
117|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
118|    spec.json                                the launch spec
119|    notes.md                                 optional: what you tried and why
120|  summary.md                                 your final attempt per slot
121|```
122|
123|`<slot-folder>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing-combine` or `experts`. Grade an attempt with:

126|.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N> <slot>

137|  ]
138|}
139|```
140|
141|List one or two targets, in the order you work on them.
142|
143|**The launch spec** (`spec.json`):
144|
145|```json
146|{
147|  "kernels": [
148|    {
149|      "name": "fused_routing",
150|      "source_block": 0,
151|      "header_block": null,
152|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
153|      "outputs": [
154|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
155|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
156|      ],
157|      "grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1],
158|      "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
159|      "template": {"T": "bfloat16"},
160|      "init_value": null,
161|      "atomic_outputs": false
162|    }
163|  ],
164|  "slot_outputs": {"inds": "inds", "weights": "weights"}
165|}
166|```
167|
168|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
169|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
170|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
171|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
172|- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
173|- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.

176|
177|## How each attempt is judged
178|
179|The pass criteria are the same as in the API-stage brief and were fixed before this session, as written here.
180|
181|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows.
182|2. **G2, correct.** It is tested on inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows.
183|   - **`routing`:** each row selects the same 4 experts. The only exception is a row whose 4th and 5th biased scores in the reference are within 1e-6 of each other; such rows are counted and reported. The weights, matched by expert, are within 1e-4 relative.
184|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element is within 2 bfloat16 units in the last place of the reference value. For values smaller than 0.001 in magnitude, the unit at 0.001 applies, so summing in a different order near zero is not a failure.
185|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
186|3. **G3, faster.** The decode step's period is the median over 3 repeats in shuffled order, with 128-token prompts, at 1, 8 and 32 requests. It must be lower than both the original model's and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code. The gap must exceed the spread between repeats.

188|**What the grader prints for an attempt** (JSON):
189|- `g1` false and the compiler's error message;
190|- or the correctness results, with counts and the worst example per check;
191|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer`: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, and `beats_compiled`.
192|
193|The piece timing runs the slot on all 20 layers' captured inputs and waits for the GPU once at the end. It takes the median of 30 repeats, per layer. It is a guide; G3 decides.
194|
195|**When a slot stops.** Work on a slot stops at the first attempt that passes G1 and G2 and beats the compiled reference in the piece timing at all three row counts, or after 5 attempts. 1|# MobileMoE Bandwidth Study
2|
3|*Written by Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), directed by surucuonur. [Who made what](../PROVENANCE.md).*
4|
5|How efficiently an inference engine turns an Apple Silicon GPU's memory bandwidth and compute into generated tokens when serving a small mixture-of-experts model.
6|
7|## Hardware limits
8|
9|**Peak bandwidth**:
10|The most bytes per second the GPU can read from unified memory, as rated by the manufacturer (about 200 GB/s on this project's M1 Pro).
11|_Avoid_: max bandwidth, memory speed
12|
13|**Peak compute**:
14|The most floating-point operations per second the GPU can perform (about 5.2 TFLOPS on the 16-core M1 Pro GPU).
15|_Avoid_: max compute, TFLOPS (as the name of the limit)
16|
17|**Achieved bandwidth**:
18|The bytes a decode step must read from memory (the weights it touches plus its share of cached attention state), divided by that step's duration.
19|_Avoid_: bandwidth usage, utilization (unqualified)
20|
21|**Arithmetic intensity**:
22|Floating-point operations performed per byte read from memory during a decode step.
23|_Avoid_: compute density, FLOPs/byte ratio
24|
25|**Ridge point**:
26|The arithmetic intensity at which peak bandwidth and peak compute meet (about 26 operations per byte here); below it a step is limited by bandwidth, above it by compute.
27|
28|**Roofline**:
29|The chart of achievable throughput against arithmetic intensity, capped by peak bandwidth on the left and peak compute on the right, with measured decode steps plotted beneath it.
30|
31|## Bottlenecks and fixes
32|
33|**Bandwidth-bound**:
34|A decode step whose achieved bandwidth is close to peak bandwidth.
35|
36|**Compute-bound**:
37|A decode step whose operation rate is close to peak compute.
38|
39|**Overhead-bound**:
40|A decode step far below both limits, because its time goes to work other than reading weights or doing arithmetic, such as launching GPU jobs, routing tokens to experts or scheduling.
41|_Avoid_: latency-bound, CPU-bound (unless the CPU specifically is the cause)
42|
43|**Bottleneck**:
44|The single cause, identified from measurements, that most limits throughput for a given workload.
45|_Avoid_: issue, slowness
46|
47|**Kernel**:
48|One program the GPU runs as a unit, such as one matrix product or one element-wise add; a decode step is a chain of hundreds of them, each with a fixed start-up cost.
49|_Avoid_: GPU job, op (for a kernel launch)
50|
51|**Occupancy**:
52|The share of the GPU's thread slots in use while it runs; low occupancy means most of the chip is idle even when the GPU counts as busy.
53|_Avoid_: GPU utilization (which only says the GPU had work)
54|
55|**Knock-out**:
56|A measurement in which one piece of the decode step is replaced by a stand-in that returns the right shape without GPU work; the time and bytes the step saves are that piece's cost.
57|_Avoid_: ablation
58|
59|**Baseline**:
60|The unmodified engine serving MobileMoE-S-QAT (int4), against which every fix is measured.
61|
62|**Fix**:
63|One change to the engine, the model code or the configuration, measured against the baseline under the same workload.
64|_Avoid_: optimization (for a change that hasn't been measured), tweak
65|
66|## Inference
67|
68|**Prefill**:
69|Processing a request's whole prompt in one pass before any token is generated.
70|
71|**Decode step**:
72|One engine iteration that produces one new token for each request it includes.
73|
74|**Decode rows**:
75|The number of requests the engine actually advanced in one decode step; the batch size that matters for the roofline.
76|_Avoid_: batch size (unqualified), concurrency
77|
78|**Client concurrency**:
79|The number of requests the benchmark client keeps in flight; it caps decode rows but does not equal them.
80|_Avoid_: batch size
81|
82|## Mixture of experts
83|
84|**Expert**:
85|One of the interchangeable feed-forward blocks in a layer; MobileMoE-S has 60 routed experts per layer.
86|
87|**Active experts**:
88|The experts the router picks for one token in one layer (4 for MobileMoE-S).
89|_Avoid_: selected experts, top-k experts
90|
91|**Distinct experts**:
92|The number of different experts used by all decode rows together in one layer during one decode step; it decides how much expert weight data the step must read.
93|_Avoid_: unique experts, expert coverage
94|
95|## Models
96|
97|**MobileMoE-S**:
98|Meta's smallest on-device mixture-of-experts model (about 1.3B parameters in total, about 272M used per token), studied here in its SFT (full-precision) and QAT (int4) variants.
99|
100|**Muse Spark**:
101|Meta's hosted model. In this project it chooses which pieces of the decode step to replace and writes their kernels, working in its own Muse Spark session; it is never the model under study.
102|
103|**Muse Code**:
104|Meta's own coding agent for the terminal, built on Muse Spark; the only program in which Muse Spark does its work in this project.
105|_Avoid_: Muse CLI, Meta Code
106|
107|**Muse Spark session**:
108|A Muse Code session in which Muse Spark writes every turn, the lead's and every helper's, kept apart from Claude's work by its own branch, folder and commit trailer.
109|_Avoid_: guardrail (for the session itself), Meta mode
110|
111|## Muse Spark's work
112|
113|**Slot**:
114|One replaceable piece of the mixture-of-experts block (routing, combine, or the routed experts), with fixed inputs and outputs, that Muse Spark may replace with its own kernels.
115|_Avoid_: target (that is a slot Muse Spark has chosen), module
116|
117|**Round**:
118|One Muse Spark session working through the round skill, followed by Claude's independent measurement of what it produced.
119|_Avoid_: iteration, cycle
120|
121|**Lead agent**:
122|The one agent in a Muse Spark session that grades kernels and commits; it starts the helpers and decides what they work on.
123|_Avoid_: orchestrator, main agent
124|
125|**Helper agent**:
126|An agent the lead starts for one bounded task (investigating one lens, drafting a design, reviewing a draft, verifying claims), which reports back and never grades or commits.
127|_Avoid_: swarm, worker, subagent (when the role matters, not the mechanism)
128|
129|**Reminder agent**:
130|One of Muse Code's own background agents, which watch the lead's progress and may nudge it, for example to check a claim before it says it is done; Muse Spark writes their turns too, but they take no part in the work.
131|_Avoid_: helper (that is one the lead starts)
132|
133|**Diagnosis**:
134|Muse Spark's written account of why each slot is slow: its cost, the kind of limit it hits, and the root cause in the code, every claim with a source.
135|_Avoid_: analysis, findings (those are Claude's)
136|
137|**Draft**:
138|A candidate kernel a helper writes for the lead to choose from; never graded on its own.
139|_Avoid_: attempt, candidate
140|
141|**Attempt**:
142|A kernel the lead has graded and committed; attempts for a slot are numbered in order and have no limit.
143|_Avoid_: try, submission

from functools import partial

import mlx.core as mx
import mlx.nn as nn


@partial(mx.compile, shapeless=True)
def swiglu(gate, x):
    return nn.silu(gate) * x


@partial(mx.compile, shapeless=True)
def xielu(x, alpha_p, alpha_n, beta, eps):
    alpha_p = nn.softplus(alpha_p)
    alpha_n = beta + nn.softplus(alpha_n)
    return mx.where(
        x > 0,
        alpha_p * mx.square(x) + beta * x,
        (mx.expm1(mx.minimum(x, eps)) - x) * alpha_n + beta * x,
    )


class XieLU(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self,
        alpha_p_init=0.8,
        alpha_n_init=0.8,
        beta=0.5,
        eps=-1e-6,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        alpha_p_tensor = mx.array(alpha_p_init)
        alpha_n_tensor = mx.array(alpha_n_init - beta)
        self.alpha_p = mx.log(mx.exp(alpha_p_tensor) - 1)
        self.alpha_n = mx.log(mx.exp(alpha_n_tensor) - 1)

        self.beta = mx.array(beta)
        self.eps = mx.array(eps)

    def __call__(self, x: mx.array) -> mx.array:
        return xielu(x, self.alpha_p, self.alpha_n, self.beta, self.eps)

194|                    for k in per_layer[0]

65|class Attention(nn.Module):
66|    def __init__(self, args: ModelArgs, use_rope: bool):
67|        super().__init__()
68|        dim = args.hidden_size
69|        self.n_heads = args.num_attention_heads
70|        self.n_kv_heads = args.num_key_value_heads
71|        self.head_dim = args.head_dim
72|        self.scale = self.head_dim**-0.5

74|        bias = args.attention_bias
75|        self.q_proj = nn.Linear(dim, self.n_heads * self.head_dim, bias=bias)
76|        self.k_proj = nn.Linear(dim, self.n_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=bias)
77|        self.v_proj = nn.Linear(dim, self.n_kv_heads * self.head_dim, bias=bias)
78|        self.o_proj = nn.Linear(self.n_heads * self.head_dim, dim, bias=bias)
79|
80|        self.use_rope = use_rope
81|        if use_rope:
82|            self.rope = initialize_rope(
83|                self.head_dim,
84|                args.rope_theta,
85|                traditional=True,
86|                scaling_config=args.rope_scaling,
87|                max_position_embeddings=args.max_position_embeddings,
88|            )
89|
90|        # The reference applies this norm after RoPE. RoPE does not change
91|        # the vector norm, so applying it before RoPE gives the same result.
92|        self.use_qk_norm = args.use_qk_norm and use_rope
93|        if self.use_qk_norm:

97|    def __call__(
98|        self,
99|        x: mx.array,
100|        mask: Optional[mx.array] = None,
101|        cache: Optional[Any] = None,
102|    ) -> mx.array:
103|        B, L, _ = x.shape
104|        queries = self.q_proj(x).reshape(B, L, self.n_heads, -1)
105|        keys = self.k_proj(x).reshape(B, L, self.n_kv_heads, -1)
106|        values = self.v_proj(x).reshape(B, L, self.n_kv_heads, -1)

116|        if self.use_rope:

142|class TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear(nn.Module):
143|    """Quantized expert weights in [E, in, out] layout, grouped along out."""
144|
145|    def __init__(
146|        self,
147|        input_dims: int,
148|        output_dims: int,

150|        group_size: int,

152|        mode: str = "affine",

157|            mx.random.uniform(

159|                high=scale,

174|            x,
175|            self["weight"],
176|            self["scales"],
177|            self.get("biases"),

187|class MoE(nn.Module):
188|    def __init__(self, args: ModelArgs):
189|        super().__init__()
190|        dim = args.hidden_size
191|        hidden = args.intermediate_size
192|        num_experts = args.num_local_experts
193|        self.top_k = args.num_experts_per_tok
194|        self.norm_topk_prob = args.norm_topk_prob
195|        self.routed_scaling_factor = args.routed_scaling_factor
196|
197|        self.router = nn.Linear(dim, num_experts, bias=False)
198|        self.expert_bias = mx.zeros((num_experts,))
199|        self.experts = SwitchGLU(dim, hidden, num_experts)
200|        if args.transposed_experts:
201|            q = args.quantization
202|            for name, dims in (
203|                ("gate_proj", (dim, hidden)),
204|                ("up_proj", (dim, hidden)),
205|                ("down_proj", (hidden, dim)),
206|            ):
207|                proj = TransposedQuantizedSwitchLinear(
208|                    *dims,
209|                    num_experts,
210|                    q["group_size"],
211|                    q["bits"],
212|                    q.get("mode", "affine"),
213|                )
214|                setattr(self.experts, name, proj)
215|        self.shared_expert = MLP(dim, args.intermediate_size_mlp)
216|
217|    def __call__(self, x: mx.array) -> mx.array:
218|        # The reference computes the router in float32.
219|        scores = mx.sigmoid(self.router(x.astype(mx.float32)))
220|
221|        # The bias changes which experts are selected, not their weights.
222|        k = self.top_k
223|        biased = scores + self.expert_bias
224|        inds = mx.argpartition(-biased, kth=k - 1, axis=-1)[..., :k]
225|        scores = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)
226|        if self.norm_topk_prob:
227|            scores = scores / (scores.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20)
228|        scores = scores * self.routed_scaling_factor
229|
230|        y = self.experts(x, inds)
231|        y = (y * scores[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(x.dtype)
232|        return y + self.shared_expert(x)

235|class DecoderLayer(nn.Module):
236|    def __init__(self, args: ModelArgs, layer_idx: int):
237|        super().__init__()
238|        self.self_attn = Attention(args, bool(args.no_rope_layers[layer_idx]))

246|        self.input_layernorm = nn.RMSNorm(args.hidden_size, eps=args.rms_norm_eps)

248|            args.hidden_size, eps=args.rms_norm_eps
249|        )

252|        self,
253|        x: mx.array,
254|        mask: Optional[mx.array] = None,
255|        cache: Optional[Any] = None,

291|        super().__init__()
292|        self.args = args
293|        self.model_type = args.model_type

298|    def __call__(
299|        self,
300|        inputs: mx.array,
301|        cache: Optional[Any] = None,
302|        input_embeddings: Optional[mx.array] = None,
303|    ) -> mx.array:
304|        out = self.model(inputs, cache, input_embeddings)
305|        if self.args.tie_word_embeddings:
306|            return self.model.embed_tokens.as_linear(out)
307|        return self.lm_head(out)

309|    def sanitize(self, weights):
310|        if self.args.tie_word_embeddings:
311|            weights.pop("lm_head.weight", None)
312|
313|        # Split the fused [E, D, 2F] gate/up tensor and use the
314|        # [E, out, in] layout of SwitchGLU.
315|        for l in range(self.args.num_hidden_layers):
316|            prefix = f"model.layers.{l}.feed_forward.experts"
317|            if f"{prefix}.gate_up_proj" in weights:
318|                gate_up = weights.pop(f"{prefix}.gate_up_proj")
319|                gate, up = mx.split(gate_up, 2, axis=-1)
320|                weights[f"{prefix}.gate_proj.weight"] = mx.swapaxes(gate, 1, 2)
321|                weights[f"{prefix}.up_proj.weight"] = mx.swapaxes(up, 1, 2)
322|            if f"{prefix}.down_proj" in weights:
323|                down = weights.pop(f"{prefix}.down_proj")
324|                weights[f"{prefix}.down_proj.weight"] = mx.swapaxes(down, 1, 2)
325|        return weights

17|- `results/runs/2026-11-01-breakdown/tables.md` and `results/runs/2026-11-02-gpu-counters/tables.md`: the raw tables;
18|- `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py` and `switch_layers.py`: the model code;
19|- MLX's custom-kernel documentation: `.venv/bin/python -c "import mlx.core as mx; help(mx.fast.metal_kernel)"`;
20|- `bench/grader/check_candidate.py` and `bench/grader/slots.py`: how you are graded.
21|
22|## The slots
23|
24|Each slot is a piece of the mixture-of-experts block, `MoE.__call__` in `mobilemoe.py`, which runs in all 20 layers of every step. `rows` is the number of tokens in the step: 1 to 32 in decode. The grader flattens the inputs to the shapes below and restores the model's shapes afterwards. All arrays are row-contiguous.
25|
26|The model's constants: hidden size `D = 768`, experts `E = 60`, experts per token `K = 4`, expert hidden size `H = 384`, `routed_scaling_factor = 2.5`, `norm_topk_prob = true`.
27|
28|### `routing`: router, top-4 selection and weights
29|
30|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
31||---|---|---|---|
32|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
33|| input | `w_router` | [60, 768] | float32 |
34|| input | `bias` | [60] | float32 (the model's bfloat16 `expert_bias`, converted exactly) |
35|| output | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
36|| output | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
37|
38|Reference:
39|
40|```python
41|scores = mx.sigmoid(x.astype(mx.float32) @ w_router.T)          # [rows, 60]
42|inds = mx.argpartition(-(scores + bias), kth=3, axis=-1)[:, :4]  # the 4 largest biased scores
43|w = mx.take_along_axis(scores, inds, axis=-1)                    # unbiased scores of those 4
44|weights = w / (w.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True) + 1e-20) * 2.5
45|```
46|
47|The order of the 4 experts within a row is free, as long as `weights[r, j]` belongs to `inds[r, j]`. Today this slot is about 12 kernels per layer, 240 per step. It costs 1.02 ms of a 4.75 ms step at 1 request and 1.68 ms at 32 requests.
48|
49|### `combine`: weighting the routed experts' outputs and adding the shared expert
50|
51|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
52||---|---|---|---|
53|| input | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 (the 4 experts' outputs, in `inds` order) |
54|| input | `weights` | [rows, 4] | float32 |
55|| input | `shared` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 (the shared expert's output) |
56|| output | `out` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
57|
58|Reference:
59|
60|```python
61|out = (y * weights[..., None]).sum(axis=-2).astype(mx.bfloat16) + shared
62|```
63|
64|Today this slot is 5 kernels per layer, 100 per step. It costs 0.61 ms at 1 request and 0.33 ms at 32 requests.
65|
66|### `routing+combine`
67|
68|Both slots above, each with its own kernels, in one candidate.
69|
70|### `experts`: the routed experts' three quantized products
71|
72|| | Name | Shape | Dtype |
73||---|---|---|---|
74|| input | `x` | [rows, 768] | bfloat16 |
75|| input | `inds` | [rows, 4] | uint32 |
76|| input | `gate_w`, `up_w` | [60, 768, 48] | uint32 (4-bit weights in [expert, in, out] layout, 8 per word along out) |
77|| input | `gate_scales`, `gate_biases`, `up_scales`, `up_biases` | [60, 768, 12] | bfloat16 (one scale and bias per 32 outputs) |
78|| input | `down_w` | [60, 384, 96] | uint32 |
79|| input | `down_scales`, `down_biases` | [60, 384, 24] | bfloat16 |
80|| output | `y` | [rows, 4, 768] | bfloat16 |
81|
82|Each weight is `w = scale * q + bias`, with `q` the 4-bit value. In MLX's affine quantization, the value for output column `o` sits in word `o / 8` at bits `4 * (o % 8)`.
83|
84|Reference: for each row `r` and each `j`, with `e = inds[r, j]`:
85|
86|```python
87|y[r, j] = (silu(x[r] @ Wgate[e]) * (x[r] @ Wup[e])) @ Wdown[e]
88|```
89|
90|As in MLX's `gather_qmm(..., transpose=False)`, each product accumulates in float32 and rounds its output to bfloat16. `silu(gate) * up` is computed on those bfloat16 values, and its result is rounded to bfloat16 before the down product.
91|
92|Today this slot is 7 kernels per layer at 1 request and 13 at 32 requests (from 16 rows, MLX also sorts the pairs by expert). It costs 0.92 ms at 1 request and 14.67 ms of a 28.19 ms step at 32 requests, half the step. It reads each expert once per (token, expert) pair.
93|
94|## Tools and limits
95|
96|- **Only `mx.fast.metal_kernel`, MLX 0.32.4.** You write the Metal body; MLX generates the signature. Inputs arrive as `const device T* name` and outputs as `device T* name`. Shapes and strides come as `name_shape` and `name_strides` when the source uses them. The thread attributes are available, as in MLX's documentation: `thread_position_in_grid`, `threadgroup_position_in_grid`, `thread_position_in_threadgroup`, `threads_per_threadgroup`, `simdgroup_index_in_threadgroup`, `thread_index_in_simdgroup`, and so on.
97|- **The grader runs no Python of yours.** It reads your launch spec as data and compiles only your Metal.
98|- **Stay within the GPU's limits.** At most 1,024 threads per threadgroup and 32 KB of threadgroup memory. A grader run should take under 3 minutes; stop one that hangs.
99|- **Hardware.** The Apple M1 Pro GPU (`applegpu_g13s`) has 16 cores and a SIMD width of 32. bfloat16 is available in Metal as `bfloat`.
100|
101|## Rules of this session
102|
103|These keep your work apart from everyone else's. Git hooks and an audit script enforce them, and a commit that breaks them is refused.
104|
105|- **Write only inside `muse-spark/`.** Never change `bench/`, `claude/`, `results/`, `tools/`, `third_party/`, or any other file. A copy of the grader you edit is never used.
106|- **Commit only on `muse-agent`,** with the co-author trailer your settings add: `Co-Authored-By: Muse Spark (Meta Model API) <muse-spark@meta-model-api.invalid>`. Start each subject with `Muse Spark:`. No other co-author.
107|- **Never push, merge, rebase, change git config, or skip hooks.**
108|- **Don't read `.env`** or any credentials file.
109|- One commit per attempt, after you've run the grader on it, so the history shows every attempt in order.
110|
111|## Your files
112|
113|```
114|muse-spark/
115|  strategy.md                                your choice and design, ending with the targets JSON
116|  kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N>/
117|    block-0.metal, block-1.metal, ...        Metal kernel bodies (and headers), numbered from 0
118|    spec.json                                the launch spec
119|    notes.md                                 optional: what you tried and why
120|  summary.md                                 your final attempt per slot
121|```
122|
123|`<slot-folder>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing-combine` or `experts`. Grade an attempt with:
124|
125|```bash
126|.venv/bin/python bench/grader/check_candidate.py muse-spark/kernels/<slot-folder>/attempt-<N> <slot>
127|```
128|
129|where `<slot>` is `routing`, `combine`, `routing+combine` or `experts`.
130|
131|**The targets JSON** at the end of `strategy.md`:
132|
133|```json
134|{
135|  "targets": [
136|    {"slot": "routing+combine", "why": "...", "expected_saving_ms": {"rows_1": 0.0, "rows_32": 0.0}, "design": "..."}
137|  ]
138|}
139|```
140|
141|List one or two targets, in the order you work on them.
142|
143|**The launch spec** (`spec.json`):
144|
145|```json
146|{
147|  "kernels": [
148|    {
149|      "name": "fused_routing",
150|      "source_block": 0,
151|      "header_block": null,
152|      "inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
153|      "outputs": [
154|        {"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
155|        {"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}
156|      ],
157|      "grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1],
158|      "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
159|      "template": {"T": "bfloat16"},
160|      "init_value": null,
161|      "atomic_outputs": false
162|    }
163|  ],
164|  "slot_outputs": {"inds": "inds", "weights": "weights"}
165|}
166|```
167|
168|- **`source_block` and `header_block`** are the numbers of your `block-N.metal` files.
169|- **Kernels run in list order.** A kernel's `inputs` may name slot inputs or outputs of earlier kernels.
170|- **`slot_outputs`** maps each output of the slot to the kernel output that provides it.
171|- **For `routing+combine`,** `spec.json` holds two specs, each in the format above for its own slot: `{"routing": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}, "combine": {"kernels": [...], "slot_outputs": {...}}}`. The original experts and shared expert run between the two parts. The grader tests each part on its own, and the combine part receives the reference routing weights.
172|- **Shape and grid entries** are integers, or products of integers and the names `rows`, `D`, `E`, `K` and `H`, such as `"rows*32"`. Nothing else is evaluated.
173|- **dtypes** are `float32`, `bfloat16`, `float16`, `uint32` or `int32`.
174|- **Template values** are one of those dtypes, an integer or a boolean.
175|- **`grid`** counts threads, not threadgroups, as in `mx.fast.metal_kernel`.
176|
177|## How each attempt is judged
178|
179|The pass criteria are the same as in the API-stage brief and were fixed before this session, as written here.
180|
181|1. **G1, runs.** It compiles and runs on real inputs at 1, 8 and 32 rows.
182|2. **G2, correct.** It is tested on inputs captured from all 20 layers during a real decode step, at 1, 8 and 32 rows.
183|   - **`routing`:** each row selects the same 4 experts. The only exception is a row whose 4th and 5th biased scores in the reference are within 1e-6 of each other; such rows are counted and reported. The weights, matched by expert, are within 1e-4 relative.
184|   - **`combine` and `experts`:** every element is within 2 bfloat16 units in the last place of the reference value. For values smaller than 0.001 in magnitude, the unit at 0.001 applies, so summing in a different order near zero is not a failure.
185|   - **Then, end to end:** the same greedy tokens as the original model over 24 generated tokens, at 1 and 32 requests, in both plain MLX and vLLM.
186|3. **G3, faster.** The decode step's period is the median over 3 repeats in shuffled order, with 128-token prompts, at 1, 8 and 32 requests. It must be lower than both the original model's and an `mx.compile` of the same reference code. The gap must exceed the spread between repeats.

191|- or, when the attempt is correct, `timing_us_per_layer`: its time per call next to the original's and the compiled reference's, and `beats_compiled`.

193|The piece timing runs the slot on all 20 layers' captured inputs and waits for the GPU once at the end. It takes the median of 30 repeats, per layer. It is a guide; G3 decides.
194|

Assembling a detailed report with MoE decoding, slot interface, system checklist, and per-file citations.

Validating MoE routing and combine logic against reference outputs with ULP tolerance checks.

# Lens 4 (round 1): System context — report

## (a) How the decode step reaches the MoE block; what runs just before/after each slot

Decode path per layer (`third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/mobilemoe.py:251-258`): `h = x + self_attn(input_layernorm(x), mask, cache)`, then `return h + feed_forward(post_attention_layernorm(h))`. So the MoE block's input is RMS-normed `h`, and its output is residual-added back to `h`. `feed_forward` is `MoE` iff `layer_idx % step == step-1` (`mobilemoe.py:240-244`); with `interleave_moe_layer_step = 1` all 20 layers are MoE (brief states "runs in all 20 layers", `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:24`).

Inside `MoE.__call__` (`mobilemoe.py:217-232`):
1. Router: `scores = sigmoid(router(x.astype(float32)))` (line 219) — float32 matmul then sigmoid.
2. Bias only selects: `biased = scores + expert_bias; inds = argpartition(-biased, kth=k-1)[..., :k]` (lines 223-224); weights are the *unbiased* scores gathered at `inds` (line 225), normalized `/(sum+1e-20)` (line 227), scaled `* 2.5` (line 228).
3. `y = experts(x, inds)` (line 230) — bfloat16 `x` at model shape, integer `inds`.
4. `y = (y*scores[...,None]).sum(-2).astype(x.dtype)` (line 231), `return y + shared_expert(x)` (line 232) where `shared_expert` is a dense SwiGLU `MLP` (`mobilemoe.py:131-139,215`).

What runs just before/after **each slot** (split form `bench/grader/slots.py:105-117`):
- **routing** (`slots.py:109`): before = `post_attention_layernorm(h)` reshape to flat `[rows,768]` + `expert_bias.astype(float32)` (lines 106-108); after = experts call consuming `inds` (lines 110-114) and combine consuming `weights` (line 116).
- **experts** (`slots.py:110-114`): before = routing (`inds`); runs concurrently with nothing — `shared_expert(x)` (line 115) is a separate branch on the same `x`; after = combine, which takes `y.reshape(-1,K,D)` in `inds` order (line 116).
- **combine** (`slots.py:116`): before = routed experts `y` + routing `weights` + dense `shared_expert(x)` branch (lines 114-115); after = reshape to `(*lead,D)` (line 117) then DecoderLayer residual add and next layer's `input_layernorm → Attention` (`mobilemoe.py:257-258,283-284`).
- Attention itself (the neighbour that dominates non-MoE time): q/k/v projs, QK RMS-norm, RoPE, `cache.update_and_fetch`, SDPA, o_proj (`mobilemoe.py:97-128`).

## (b) What a replacement must keep identical

| Item | Constraint | Source |
|---|---|---|
| routing `inds` | same set of 4 experts per row; order within row free. Only exception: row whose reference 4th/5th biased scores differ by < 1e-6 (counted as tie, not failure) | `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:68-80`, `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:183` |
| routing `weights` | matched **by expert** (`ref = dict(zip(ref_inds[r], ref_w[r]))`), relative err `|v-ref|/max(|ref|,1e-12)` ≤ 1e-4 | `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:81-87,137` |
| routing shapes/dtypes | `inds [rows,4] uint32`, `weights [rows,4] float32`; `inds < 60` | `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:54-66` |
| combine/experts tolerance | every element within 2 bf16 ULPs of reference; ULP floored at `|r|=0.001` (`ulp = 2^(floor(log2(max(|r|,1e-3)))-7)`) | `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:44-47,101-109,119-130,138` |
| combine shape/dtype | `out [rows,768] bfloat16` | `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:99-100` |
| experts shape/dtype | `y [rows,4,768] bfloat16`, in `inds` order (slot `j` ↔ `inds[r,j]`; error message indexes "expert slot k") | `bench/grader/check_candidate.py:117-129`, `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:53` |
| combine rounding point | weighted sum in float, `.astype(bfloat16)` **before** `+ shared` | `bench/grader/slots.py:52`, `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:61` |
| experts rounding points | each `gather_qmm` accumulates float32, rounds to bf16; `silu(gate)*up` computed on those bf16 values and rounded to bf16 before down-proj | `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:90`, `bench/grader/slots.py:79` + `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/activations.py:9-11` (`silu(gate)*x`) |
| experts quant | `w = scale*q + bias`, 4-bit `q` at word `o/8`, bits `4*(o%8)`, `group_size=32, bits=4, mode=affine, transpose=False` | `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:82`, `bench/grader/slots.py:68-77` |
| experts sort | no observable constraint — sort at `inds.size >= 64` is an unbinding perf choice; outputs identical either way | `bench/grader/slots.py:62-65,80-82`, `third_party/mlx-lm/mlx_lm/models/switch_layers.py:181` |
| end-to-end | same greedy tokens over 24 tokens at 1 and 32 requests, plain MLX and vLLM (run after merge, not by piece grader) | `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:185` |

## (c) Grader slot interface in full detail

Constants: `D,E,K,H = 768,60,4,384`, `SCALE = 2.5` (`bench/grader/slots.py:19-20`). Slot I/O (`slots.py:29-40`): routing `["x","w_router","bias"] → ["inds","weights"]`; combine `["y","weights","shared"] → ["out"]`; experts `["x","inds", gate/up/down × w/scales/biases] → ["y"]`; `routing+combine` concatenates routing inputs + `["y","shared"]` → `["inds","weights","out"]`. Expert weight shapes/dtypes per brief table (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:72-80`): `gate_w/up_w [60,768,48] uint32`, scales/biases `[60,768,12] bf16`, `down_w [60,384,96] uint32`, scales/biases `[60,384,24] bf16`.

Inputs: captured from one real decode step — random 128-token prefill (`randint(0,100000,(rows,128))`), `step-1` greedy tokens, hooks record every layer (`slots.py:137-171`); saved at rows 1/8/32 with bf16 stored as float32 in `models/muse-inputs/rows{rows}.npz` as `L{i:02d}_{k}` (`slots.py:174-186`); loader restores bf16 for `x,y,shared`, renames `weights_in→weights`, casts `inds→uint32`, optionally merges served-checkpoint expert weights (`slots.py:205-223`).

G1: spec builds via `slots.build` (raises = G1 fail, compiler error lines kept, ≤4000 chars, `check_candidate.py:153-163,227-228`) and runs at 1/8/32 rows. G2: per-layer checks aggregated (`max` for `max*`, `sum` else; `pass` = all layers pass; first `worst_example` kept; `g2` = all pass, `check_candidate.py:187-208`). Timing (only if G2): per rows count, per part, `reference + mx.compile(reference) + candidate` µs/layer summed; `timed` = 3 warmups then median of 30 repeats of all-20-layers + one GPU wait (`check_candidate.py:141-150,209-226`); `beats_compiled` requires candidate < compiled at **all** of 1/8/32.

Launch spec (`slots.py:251-293`, brief `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:143-175`): `spec.json` + `block-N.metal` (sorted numerically, `check_candidate.py:36-39`). Each kernel: `name` (non-word chars → `_`), `source_block`/`header_block` (int or null), `inputs` (slot inputs or earlier kernels' outputs, run in list order), `outputs` (`name/shape/dtype`), `grid` (**threads**, not threadgroups), `threadgroup` (each ≥1, product ≤1024 or ValueError), `template` (dtype/int/bool only), `init_value`, `atomic_outputs`. Sizes are ints or `*`-products of ints and `rows/D/E/K/H` (`slots.py:226-240`); dtypes from `{float32,bfloat16,float16,uint32,int32}` (`slots.py:22-28,243-248`). `slot_outputs` must cover every slot output (`slots.py:266-268,291`). `rows` is taken from the first slot input's `shape[0]` (`slots.py:271`). For `routing+combine`, `spec.json` is `{"routing": {...}, "combine": {...}}`, each part built/tested/timed independently, combine fed **reference** routing weights, original experts+shared run between (`check_candidate.py:40-41`, `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:171`).

Example spec (routing, from brief `claude/muse-agent-brief.md:145-166`):
```json
{"kernels": [{"name": "fused_routing", "source_block": 0, "header_block": null,
"inputs": ["x", "w_router", "bias"],
"outputs": [{"name": "inds", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "uint32"},
{"name": "weights", "shape": ["rows", 4], "dtype": "float32"}],
"grid": ["rows*32", 1, 1], "threadgroup": [32, 1, 1],
"template": {"T": "bfloat16"}, "init_value": null, "atomic_outputs": false}],
"slot_outputs": {"inds": "inds", "weights": "weights"}}
```
Grid arithmetic example: at rows=32, `"rows*32"` → `dim("rows*32",32) = 32*32 = 1024` threads (`slots.py:230-240`); with threadgroup 32 → 32 threadgroups.

Limits: MLX 0.32.4 `mx.fast.metal_kernel` only; inputs `const device T*`, outputs `device T*`, `name_shape`/`name_strides` on use, thread attributes available (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:96`); ≤1024 threads/threadgroup, ≤32 KB threadgroup memory, run < 3 min (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:98`); M1 Pro `applegpu_g13s`, 16 cores, SIMD32, Metal `bfloat` (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:99`); `metal_kernel` defaults `ensure_row_contiguous=True`, `math_mode="safe"` (`.venv` help text). Grader runs no Python of the candidate — spec is data, only Metal compiles (`claude/muse-agent-brief.md:97`).

## System-aware checklist per piece of code

**P1. `ref_routing` (`bench/grader/slots.py:44-48`)**: Callers: `make_moe_call` default (line 97,109), `check_routing` (line 51 of check_candidate), `capture.recording_routing` (slots.py:149-152). Callees: `sigmoid`, fp32 matmul, `argpartition(kth=3)`, `take_along_axis`. Data: `x [rows,768] bf16`, `w_router [60,768] f32`, `bias [60] f32` → `inds [rows,4]`, `weights [rows,4] f32`. Neighbours: flat reshape + bias cast before; experts/combine after (slots.py:106-116). Cost: ~12 kernels/layer, 240/step; 1.02/4.75 ms @1 req, 1.68 ms @32 (brief line 47). Invariants: bias affects selection only (unbiased scores gathered, `mobilemoe.py:221-225`); normalize `/(sum+1e-20)`, scale 2.5; within-row expert order free (brief line 47).

**P2. `ref_combine` (`slots.py:51-52`)**: Callers: `make_moe_call` (line 97,116), `check_combine`, `capture.recording_combine` (slots.py:154-156). Callees: elementwise mul/sum/cast/add. Data: `y [rows,4,768] bf16`, `weights [rows,4] f32`, `shared [rows,768] bf16` → `out [rows,768] bf16`. Neighbours: routed experts + shared-MLP branch before; reshape + residual + next-layer attn-norm after. Cost: 5 kernels/layer, 100/step; 0.61 ms @1, 0.33 ms @32 (brief line 64). Invariants: cast to bf16 **before** adding shared; `y` slots align with `inds` order.

**P3. `ref_experts` (`slots.py:55-82`) + `SwitchGLU` (`switch_layers.py:160-199`) + `swiglu` (`activations.py:9-11`)**: Callers: `make_moe_call(experts=...)` (slots.py:113-114), `check_experts`, identity check (slots.py:127). Callees: `expand_dims(-2,-3)`, `_gather_sort`/`_scatter_unsort` (switch_layers.py:12-24), 3× `gather_qmm(group32/bits4/affine/transpose=False)`, `swiglu = silu(gate)*x`. Data: flat `[rows,768] bf16` + `[rows,4]` inds + 9 weight arrays → `[rows,4,768] bf16`. Neighbours: routing before; combine + shared branch after. Cost: 7 kernels/layer @1 req, 13 @32 (sort from 16 rows); 0.92 ms @1, 14.67/28.19 ms @32 (brief line 92); reads each expert per (token,expert) pair. Invariants: f32 accumulate → bf16 round per qmm; activation on bf16, re-rounded pre-down (brief line 90); sort threshold `inds.size>=64` unobservable.

**P4. `make_moe_call` (`slots.py:97-119`) + `check_identity` (`slots.py:122-134`)**: Callers: capture, identity check. Callees: routing/experts/combine slots, `expert_weights` (slots.py:88-94), `shared_expert`. Data: model-shaped `x` ↔ flat `[rows,768]`; `bias = expert_bias.astype(f32)` exact (bf16→f32). Neighbours: `DecoderLayer` residual/norms outside. Cost: zero — wiring only. Invariants: with references, bit-identical to port at 1/8/32 rows (`array_equal`, line 131), so all deltas come from swapped slots.

**P5. `capture/save_inputs/load_inputs/load_expert_weights` (`slots.py:137-223`)**: Callers: `main` (capture→identity→save), grader `main`/`timed`. Callees: `bd.prefill/greedy`, `make_prompt_cache`, `load_model`, `gpu_lock.hold`. Data: `rows{1,8,32}.npz`, keys `L{i:02d}_{k}`, bf16-as-f32 + `weights_in` naming. Neighbours: real decode step with KV cache; 20 layers × 3 row counts. Cost: one-time capture. Invariants: seed defaults to rows; `mx.eval(logits, seen)` forces materialization (line 168); loader restores dtypes/names exactly.

**P6. `build` (`slots.py:251-293`)**: Callers: grader `load` (`check_candidate.py:34-41`). Callees: `mx.fast.metal_kernel` per kernel. Data: spec dict + Metal sources → `run(**slot_inputs) → slot_outputs`; env chains kernel outputs forward (line 290). Neighbours: `DIM/NAMES/DTYPES` validators. Cost: compile once per attempt. Invariants: kernels in list order; threadgroup product ≤1024; grid in threads; missing slot_outputs → ValueError.

**P7. `check_routing`+`passes` (`check_candidate.py:50-93,133-138`)**: Callers: grader main loop (lines 181-187). Callees: `ref_routing`, numpy sort. Data: per-layer `{rows_wrong_experts, near_tie_rows, max_rel_err, [example]}`. Neighbours: shape/dtype/range gates precede value checks. Cost: CPU-side, all 20 layers × 3 row counts. Invariants: set-compare experts; tie band `biased[3]-biased[4] < 1e-6`; pass = 0 wrong + rel err ≤1e-4.

**P8. `check_combine` (`check_candidate.py:96-109`)**: as P7; Data: `{max_ulp, bad, [example row/col]}`; Invariants: `bad = (over>2).sum()`, pass = `bad==0`; NaN/inf → 1e9 (lines 103-104).

**P9. `check_experts` (`check_candidate.py:112-130`)**: as P8 with reshape to `[rows,-1]`; example decodes expert-slot `k` and column `d` via `divmod(j,768)` (line 126).

**P10. `timed` + timing verdict (`check_candidate.py:141-150,209-226`)**: Callers: grader main (only if G2). Callees: candidate fn, `REFERENCE[part]`, `mx.compile(REFERENCE[part])`. Data: `timing_us_per_layer["rows N"] = {reference, compiled, candidate}`; `beats_compiled` = strict `<` at all 3 counts. Neighbours: guide only — G3 (median-of-3 step period, must beat original AND compiled beyond repeat spread) decides (brief lines 186,193). Cost: 30 repeats × 3 row counts. Invariants: warmup 3×; single GPU wait per repeat over all 20 layers.

**P11. Decode skeleton `DecoderLayer`/`MobileMoEModel`/`Model` (`mobilemoe.py:235-307`)**: Callers: `bd.prefill`/greedy loop, vLLM serving. Callees: Attention, MoE/MLP, RMSNorms, embedding/lm_head. Data: `[B,L,768]` bf16 activations; KV cache across steps. Neighbours: step = ~870-1090 kernels, far from bandwidth/compute limits (brief line 9). Cost: full-step context for slot savings (routing 1.02/1.68 ms, combine 0.61/0.33 ms, experts 0.92/14.67 ms). Invariants: pre-norm + dual residuals; tied embeddings by default; `sanitize` splits fused gate/up and swaps to `[E,out,in]` (lines 309-325).

**P12. `mx.fast.metal_kernel` tool (`.venv` help + brief lines 96-99)**: Callers: `slots.build`. Callees: Metal compiler. Data: `(name, input_names, output_names, source, header, ensure_row_contiguous=True, atomic_outputs, compile_options.math_mode="safe")` → callable taking `(inputs, template, grid, threadgroup, output_shapes, output_dtypes, init_value)`. Neighbours: MLX graph (row-contiguous enforced). Cost: kernel-launch overhead is the enemy (hundreds of tiny kernels/step). Invariants: signature auto-generated; thread attrs available; ≤1024 threads/threadgroup, ≤32 KB threadgroup mem; SIMD32; `bfloat` supported.
